component.name: Apache ZooKeeper
component.description: Open-source coordination service for distributed applications (naming, synchronization, group services). ZooKeeper is intended for use inside a trusted network, not exposed directly to the Internet: the Admin Guide states that a ZooKeeper ensemble is expected to operate in a trusted computing environment and recommends deploying behind a firewall. A fresh ensemble ships with no transport encryption, no peer authentication, and world-readable/writable znodes; hardening is a shared responsibility between the project and the operator, and the documented security controls are opt-in.

externalReferences.comment: Source security page (security model, opt-in controls, scope, and vulnerability reports); this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: ZooKeeper ensemble deployment
blueprints.description: Deployment shape implied by the security model: an ensemble of ZooKeeper servers operating in a trusted computing environment behind a firewall; clients (and the Java client library) connect to the client port; ensemble members exchange quorum and election traffic; the AdminServer exposes an HTTP administration interface. Security support covers the core server, the Java client library, and the AdminServer published to Maven Central under org.apache.zookeeper.

assets.name: ZooKeeper server
assets.description: The core coordination server holding the znode data tree and serving client requests; supports opt-in TLS, opt-in client authentication (digest, SASL/Kerberos, x509/mTLS), and per-znode ACLs.

assets.name: Znode data tree and ACLs
assets.description: Hierarchical znodes protected by per-znode ACLs using the world, auth, digest, sasl, ip, or x509 schemes. ACLs are not applied automatically and are not recursive; unless the application sets a restrictive ACL, nodes are commonly created with the wide-open OPEN_ACL_UNSAFE (world:anyone with all permissions).

assets.name: AdminServer
assets.description: HTTP administration interface. Its default client IP detection honors the X-Forwarded-For header, which can be forged to bypass IP-based access controls (CVE-2024-51504); operators exposing it should configure a trusted proxy or restrict access at the network layer.

assets.name: Java client library
assets.description: The supported client library published under org.apache.zookeeper; in scope for security reports. The C CLI example shells (cli_st, cli_mt) are sample code, not production tools.

zones.name: Network clients
zones.description: Applications and administrators connecting to the client port and the AdminServer from within the trusted network the ensemble is expected to operate in.

zones.name: ZooKeeper ensemble
zones.description: The ZooKeeper servers, their data tree, and the AdminServer, expected to operate in a trusted computing environment behind a firewall.

zones.name: Quorum peers
zones.description: Other ensemble members exchanging quorum and election traffic; peer authentication (SASL or TLS) is opt-in, and firewalling the election/quorum channel is the documented mitigation when it is off.

assumptions.description: A ZooKeeper ensemble is expected to operate in a trusted computing environment and is recommended to be deployed behind a firewall; it is not exposed directly to the Internet.
The default configuration is intentionally minimal: no transport encryption, no peer authentication, and world-readable/writable znodes until the operator enables the opt-in controls.
Network-level controls prevent IP address forgery on any path that relies on the spoofable ip ACL scheme.

threats.name: Bypass of an enabled and correctly configured security control
threats.description: Bypass of an enabled, correctly configured control is in scope for private security reports: for example authentication bypass when SASL is on, ACL enforcement bugs, or behaviors that contradict documented guarantees. Historical instances include the SASL quorum peer authorization bypass via an instance-less auth ID (CVE-2023-44981), the missing ACL check on persistent watchers (CVE-2024-23944), the getACL() disclosure of digest credentials (CVE-2019-0201), and the AdminServer snapshot/restore permission check (CVE-2025-58457).

threats.name: Attacks on an unhardened default ensemble
threats.description: A fresh ensemble ships with no transport encryption, no peer authentication, and world-readable/writable znodes. Missing hardening on a default installation is expected behavior, not a vulnerability: the default configuration is intentionally minimal, and absence of encryption or authentication on a fresh ensemble is out of scope for security reports. Operators deploy behind a firewall and enable the opt-in controls.

threats.name: Arbitrary endpoint joining the quorum
threats.description: Without quorum peer authentication (opt-in, off by default), an arbitrary endpoint could join the cluster and begin propagating counterfeit changes to the leader, gaining complete read-write access to the data tree (CVE-2018-8012 class; CVE-2023-44981 was a bypass of the enabled control). Mitigations: enable quorum peer mutual authentication (SASL or TLS), or ensure the ensemble election/quorum communication is protected by a firewall.

threats.name: Child znodes unprotected by a parent's ACL
threats.description: ACLs are not recursive: an ACL on a parent znode does not protect its children, and each znode's ACL must be set independently. A known limitation of the access-control model, by design.

threats.name: Spoofing of the ip ACL scheme
threats.description: The ip ACL scheme matches source IP address and is spoofable, by design. Operators must ensure network-level controls prevent IP address forgery on any path that relies on this scheme.

threats.name: X-Forwarded-For forgery against AdminServer IP-based access control
threats.description: The AdminServer's default client IP detection honors the X-Forwarded-For header, which can be forged by an attacker to bypass IP-based access controls (see CVE-2024-51504); a known limitation of the default configuration, by design. Operators exposing the AdminServer should configure a trusted proxy or restrict access at the network layer.

threats.name: Weak credential protection in the digest scheme
threats.description: The digest scheme transmits the password during authentication and stores an unsalted SHA-1 hash, by design (CVE-2019-0201 showed the hash could additionally be disclosed via getACL()). Use SASL/Kerberos or mTLS where credential confidentiality is required.

threats.name: Unsupported components and indirect dependency findings
threats.description: Out of scope for private disclosure: zookeeper-contrib and zookeeper-recipes (community contributions not published to Maven Central, no security support commitment); the C CLI example shells cli_st and cli_mt (sample code illustrating C client usage, not production tools, see CVE-2016-5017; use the supported Java CLI); and third-party dependency CVEs bundled in a distribution that pose no direct exploit path through ZooKeeper (handled via public JIRA or the dev list instead).

trustBoundaries.name: Client port trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Clients reach the server and the AdminServer from the surrounding network. The ensemble is expected to sit in a trusted computing environment behind a firewall; transport encryption, client authentication, and znode ACLs are all opt-in controls at this boundary.

trustBoundaries.name: Quorum channel trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Ensemble members exchange quorum and election traffic. Peer authentication (SASL or TLS for quorum peers) is opt-in; when it is off, firewalling the election/quorum communication is the documented mitigation against counterfeit peers.

controls.name: Deploy behind a firewall in a trusted network
controls.description: Deploy the ensemble behind a firewall in a trusted computing environment, not exposed directly to the Internet; protect the election/quorum communication and prevent IP address forgery on paths relying on the ip ACL scheme.

controls.name: Enable transport encryption (TLS)
controls.description: TLS for client-server and quorum traffic, with optional hostname verification. Disabled by default; must be explicitly enabled.

controls.name: Enable client authentication
controls.description: Client authentication via digest (username/password), SASL/Kerberos, or x509/mTLS. None are enabled by default.

controls.name: Enable quorum peer authentication
controls.description: SASL or TLS authentication for quorum peers, so an arbitrary endpoint cannot join the cluster; not enabled by default.

controls.name: Set restrictive per-znode ACLs
controls.description: Per-znode ACLs using the world, auth, digest, sasl, ip, or x509 schemes. ACLs are not applied automatically and are not recursive: applications must set a restrictive ACL on each znode independently instead of the wide-open OPEN_ACL_UNSAFE default, and ensure the root ACL does not provide open permissions.

controls.name: Protect the AdminServer
controls.description: Operators exposing the AdminServer should configure a trusted proxy or restrict access at the network layer, since the default client IP detection honors the forgeable X-Forwarded-For header. Individual commands can be disabled (for example admin.snapshot.enabled and admin.restore.enabled) or the whole interface turned off via admin.enableServer.

controls.name: Prefer SASL/Kerberos or mTLS over digest
controls.description: Use SASL/Kerberos or x509/mTLS instead of the digest scheme where credential confidentiality is required; digest transmits the password during authentication and stores an unsalted SHA-1 hash.
